cells.tense: The imagining has been felt through, and the satisfaction has already arrived in it.
cells.act: move at the pace your feeling can sustain
cells.ask: Take the work you are deepest in and carry it this week at a rate your own feeling can hold past a month — no surge on it, no stall.
cells.core:
The work under your hands is finished enough to trust, and the making and the feeling are running level. What you imagined, you have felt to the far end of, and the calm is not a prize at the finish — it is the temperature of the room. No force is on anything, and nothing is left sitting.

Keeping that rhythm is the work now. Your feeling sets the direction, and taking it faster than it can go is what breaks it. Stay with the one piece and carry it at a rate you could hold a month out, and the momentum belongs to you rather than to the urgency.
cells.sheetLine: You move at the pace your feelings can carry.
cells.verb: feeling what you imagined all the way to the end of it
cells.place: the point where one thing is finished enough to leave by

cells.tense: A completion is being forced, and the imagining is being driven to arrive ahead of itself.
cells.ask: Tend the thing you keep driving to done: give it what it actually needs, at the rate it is actually moving, and keep your hands open.
cells.core:
There is something in your hands you keep bringing toward done before it is ripe, and each push needs another push. The satisfaction you are reaching for stays a step past your fingertips. The imagining is real; the timing is what got forced. What is growing here does not need more will — it needs care at the rate it actually moves.

Let up on the demand and stay close to the thing. Give it steady attention, what it needs when it needs it, without gripping it into a shape before it is ready. Hands that don't clutch and care that doesn't exhaust allow a thing to come to its own ending. Then the finish arrives because it arrived, not because you argued it into being.
cells.sheetLine: You are finishing something before it has grown.

cells.tense: Something was imagined and felt through once, and that door has stood behind you since.
cells.act: keep the truth a while before saying it
cells.ask: Choose something you made and walked past. Sit with it a week before you tell anyone or start the next thing — let it reach you first.
cells.core:
Something got made or lived through, and you stepped past it without letting it reach you. The imagining that once moved through you has gone quiet, and the satisfaction that belonged to it went by unclaimed. You stand near a door you already walked through. What is closed over is your own arrival at what you did.

Give the finished thing its due. Take a piece of your own work and stay with it a while before you speak of it or begin the next one. Let yourself register that it happened, and happened through you. Nothing needs to be pushed into the hollow; it fills once the made thing is seen by you first.
cells.sheetLine: You finished something and never let it land.
cells.verb: feeling what you imagined all the way to the end of it
cells.place: the point where one thing is finished enough to leave by

cells.tense: The weighing of what is done is already yours, and you are calling it luck.
cells.act: sort what matters from what does not, carefully
cells.ask: When you catch yourself weighing what is worth keeping and what isn't, go slower than usual until the judging hand is visible — then decide and know you decided.
cells.core:
The call on when a thing is finished and what to carry forward is already in your hands, and you don't count it as yours. You speak of it as something that simply became clear. There is craft in that weighing — which made thing is worth bringing into what comes next, and which has already given what it had. The craft is running. It is not signed.

Hone the attention rather than the output. The next time you find yourself weighing a finished piece and its worth, slow the moment down until you can see the hand doing the weighing. Sort carefully, and stay aware while you do. Doing it knowingly changes nothing about the work and everything about whose it is.
